report.incidentSummary: At market open on 2026-09-28 at 09:15 IST (03:45 UTC), stock order placements experienced high latency and failures with HTTP 503 errors. While initially suspected to be external broker API rate limiting or degradation similar to past incidents, investigation revealed that order-service exhausted its internal HTTP client connection pool to broker-connector (all 20/20 connections busy), causing 423 order requests to time out waiting to acquire a connection. This pool constriction was caused by change CHG-48221 deployed after market close on Friday 2026-09-25, which reduced broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20.
report.rootCauseStatement: Configuration change CHG-48221 reduced order-service's HTTP client connection pool limit to broker-connector (broker_client.max_connections_per_host) tenfold from 200 to 20. During the Monday market open surge at 09:15 IST (03:45 UTC)—the first high-volume trading burst under this configuration—the 20 client connections were immediately saturated, causing incoming order requests to time out waiting for an available client pool connection.

hypotheses.cause: HTTP client connection pool starvation on order-service towards broker-connector due to premature reduction of max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20
hypotheses.rationale: Change CHG-48221 reduced max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20 on Friday evening. Market open on Monday morning generated a burst of traffic (broker-connector request rate surged to 317.3 req/s), immediately saturating all 20 connections and generating 423 logged HTTP 503 errors stating 'timed out waiting for a connection to broker-connector (client pool 20/20 busy)'.

hypotheses.cause: External broker API rate limiting or upstream degradation during market open auction
hypotheses.rationale: Though past incidents PIR-2006 and PIR-2018 exhibited similar symptoms due to broker API rate limits and 5xx errors, broker-connector metrics showed p95 orders latency of only 206.7 ms at 03:45 UTC, rate_limited_count of 0 at 03:45 UTC, normal error rates (~0.32%), and zero ERROR logs from broker-connector.

hypotheses.cause: Database connection pool exhaustion or database lock contention during opening order burst
hypotheses.rationale: The primary database showed steady active connections (175.5), negligible lock wait time (4.03 ms), normal CPU utilization (36.11%), flat query volume, and order-service's database connection pool wait time peaked at only 5.57 ms.

facts.statement: On Friday 2026-09-25T13:00:00.000Z (18:30 IST), change CHG-48221 reduced order-service config broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20 to align with service mesh defaults.

Between 2026-09-28T03:45:02.512Z and 04:18:59.345Z, order-service emitted 423 ERROR logs with status 503 stating 'order <ref> failed: timed out waiting for a connection to broker-connector (client pool 20/20 busy)'.
All 423 ERROR logs recorded on order-service across the investigation window matched this single connection pool saturation error pattern.
order-service connects synchronously to broker-connector with a 2000 ms timeout, 0 retries, and an HTTP client pool limit of max 20 connections per host.
broker-connector upstream p95 latency for orders was 206.7 ms at 03:45 UTC, and its error rate remained low at 0.32% during market open.
broker-connector rate_limited_count on the orders endpoint was 0 count/min at 03:45 UTC, peaking at only 0.6 count/min at 04:10 UTC.
Database active connections, lock wait time, CPU utilization, and slow queries remained flat and normal throughout the 03:45 UTC order surge.
order-service database pool wait time peaked at 5.57 ms at 03:45 UTC with mean of 3.03 ms.

inferences.statement: Because CHG-48221 was applied on Friday evening after market close, Monday 2026-09-28 09:15 IST (03:45 UTC) was the first market open trading burst subjected to the reduced connection pool limit of 20.
Order failures were not caused by downstream broker-connector or external broker-api degradation, as upstream latency remained around 200 ms and no rate limit spikes occurred.

A pool limit of 20 concurrent connections is insufficient to support market open request rates (which reached 317.3 req/s at broker-connector), causing order-service's internal connection pool wait queue to exceed its timeout threshold.

assumptions.statement: Market open order volume on Monday morning is substantially higher than weekend or off-market hours trading activity.

timeline.event: Change CHG-48221 completed on order-service, reducing broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20.
Indian stock markets open; order traffic surges, reaching 317.3 req/s at broker-connector.
First HTTP 503 error logged on order-service: timed out waiting for connection to broker-connector with client pool 20/20 busy.
423 stock order requests fail on order-service due to internal HTTP client pool saturation.
Last HTTP 503 client pool timeout error recorded on order-service as opening order volume subsides.

confidence.rationale: Direct and exact match between configuration change CHG-48221 (reducing broker client pool to 20), service dependency definition (max 20 connections per host), and order-service's explicit ERROR logs citing 'client pool 20/20 busy'. Downstream broker and database metrics firmly rule out external degradation.

gaps.impact: Minimal impact; subsequent tool queries in round 0 (ev_19 to ev_24) retrieved the necessary broker-connector metrics and logs to evaluate upstream latency, error rate, and rate limits.

recommendedActions.action: Revert CHG-48221 or increase order-service configuration broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 20 back to 200 (or appropriately scaled capacity based on peak open concurrency).
recommendedActions.rationale: 20 connections is severely inadequate for market open peak concurrency (~300+ req/s), as demonstrated by 100% pool saturation and 423 timed-out orders.
recommendedActions.verification: Deploy updated configuration, verify client pool in-use metrics do not reach 100% capacity during market open bursts, and confirm zero 503 pool wait timeout errors in order-service logs.

recommendedActions.action: Establish load testing and capacity benchmarking requirements for connection pool setting changes prior to deploying to production tier-1 trading services.
recommendedActions.rationale: Standardizing service mesh connection limits across services without validating peak market open throughput risks recurring burst capacity failures.
recommendedActions.verification: Review deployment checklist and CI/CD policy requiring performance testing against market-open burst profiles for dependency connection configurations.

recommendedActions.action: Add specific alerting on order-service for HTTP client connection pool utilization exceeding 80% and connection pool acquire timeouts.
recommendedActions.rationale: Currently, client pool exhaustion manifested only as downstream 503 errors and was initially misattributed to external broker downtime.
recommendedActions.verification: Trigger test alert in staging when client pool saturation exceeds threshold and ensure on-call receives accurate diagnostic alert.

report.justification: Although the investigation halted due to deadline without critic review, the evidence conclusive links the failure to change CHG-48221. order-service's error logs explicitly cite 'client pool 20/20 busy', exactly matching the 20-connection limit set in CHG-48221 and the dependency graph. Downstream broker-connector metrics simultaneously rule out broker degradation.

findings.summary: The primary database did not experience any spikes in active_connections, db_lock_wait_ms, cpu_utilization, or slow queries during the order surge at 03:45 UTC. observations.statement: The primary database active_connections metric remained stable throughout the investigation window (mean 175.8, min 159.7, max 193.1), measuring 175.5 at 03:45 UTC, with no spike during the market open order surge.

Database cpu_utilization remained normal between 33.76% and 40.22% (mean 36.9%), measuring 36.11% at 03:45 UTC, showing no CPU exhaustion or spike.
Database slow_queries_per_min averaged 2.87 across the window (min 0, max 7), with 4 slow queries at 03:45 UTC, well within normal baseline noise.
Database request_rate stayed flat at ~4,000 queries/s (mean 4033 queries/s, 3886 queries/s at 03:45 UTC) and logs recorded zero ERROR-level entries across the 2-hour window.
The primary database was healthy and unstressed at 03:45 UTC; database connection pool exhaustion, slow queries, and lock contention are ruled out as the cause of order placement failures.

hypotheses.rationale: Though past incidents PIR-2006 and PIR-2018 exhibited similar symptoms due to broker API rate limits and 5xx errors, broker-connector metrics showed p95 orders latency of only 206.7 ms at 03:45 UTC, rate_limited_count of 0 at 03:45 UTC, normal error rates (~0.32%), and zero ERROR logs from broker-connector.

facts.statement: On Friday 2026-09-25T13:00:00.000Z (18:30 IST), change CHG-48221 reduced order-service config broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20 to align with service mesh defaults.

Between 2026-09-28T03:45:02.512Z and 04:18:59.345Z, order-service emitted 423 ERROR logs with status 503 stating 'order <ref> failed: timed out waiting for a connection to broker-connector (client pool 20/20 busy)'.
All 423 ERROR logs recorded on order-service across the investigation window matched this single connection pool saturation error pattern.
order-service connects synchronously to broker-connector with a 2000 ms timeout, 0 retries, and an HTTP client pool limit of max 20 connections per host.
broker-connector upstream p95 latency for orders was 206.7 ms at 03:45 UTC, and its error rate remained low at 0.32% during market open.
broker-connector rate_limited_count on the orders endpoint was 0 count/min at 03:45 UTC, peaking at only 0.6 count/min at 04:10 UTC.
Database active connections, lock wait time, CPU utilization, and slow queries remained flat and normal throughout the 03:45 UTC order surge.
order-service database pool wait time peaked at 5.57 ms at 03:45 UTC with mean of 3.03 ms.

inferences.statement: Because CHG-48221 was applied on Friday evening after market close, Monday 2026-09-28 09:15 IST (03:45 UTC) was the first market open trading burst subjected to the reduced connection pool limit of 20.
Order failures were not caused by downstream broker-connector or external broker-api degradation, as upstream latency remained around 200 ms and no rate limit spikes occurred.

A pool limit of 20 concurrent connections is insufficient to support market open request rates (which reached 317.3 req/s at broker-connector), causing order-service's internal connection pool wait queue to exceed its timeout threshold.

assumptions.statement: Market open order volume on Monday morning is substantially higher than weekend or off-market hours trading activity.

timeline.event: Change CHG-48221 completed on order-service, reducing broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20.
Indian stock markets open; order traffic surges, reaching 317.3 req/s at broker-connector.
First HTTP 503 error logged on order-service: timed out waiting for connection to broker-connector with client pool 20/20 busy.
423 stock order requests fail on order-service due to internal HTTP client pool saturation.
Last HTTP 503 client pool timeout error recorded on order-service as opening order volume subsides.

confidence.rationale: Direct and exact match between configuration change CHG-48221 (reducing broker client pool to 20), service dependency definition (max 20 connections per host), and order-service's explicit ERROR logs citing 'client pool 20/20 busy'. Downstream broker and database metrics firmly rule out external degradation.

recommendedActions.action: Revert CHG-48221 or increase order-service configuration broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 20 back to 200 (or appropriately scaled capacity based on peak open concurrency).
recommendedActions.rationale: 20 connections is severely inadequate for market open peak concurrency (~300+ req/s), as demonstrated by 100% pool saturation and 423 timed-out orders.
recommendedActions.verification: Deploy updated configuration, verify client pool in-use metrics do not reach 100% capacity during market open bursts, and confirm zero 503 pool wait timeout errors in order-service logs.

recommendedActions.action: Establish load testing and capacity benchmarking requirements for connection pool setting changes prior to deploying to production tier-1 trading services.
recommendedActions.rationale: Standardizing service mesh connection limits across services without validating peak market open throughput risks recurring burst capacity failures.
recommendedActions.verification: Review deployment checklist and CI/CD policy requiring performance testing against market-open burst profiles for dependency connection configurations.

recommendedActions.action: Add specific alerting on order-service for HTTP client connection pool utilization exceeding 80% and connection pool acquire timeouts.
recommendedActions.rationale: Currently, client pool exhaustion manifested only as downstream 503 errors and was initially misattributed to external broker downtime.
recommendedActions.verification: Trigger test alert in staging when client pool saturation exceeds threshold and ensure on-call receives accurate diagnostic alert.

payload.markdown:
# Investigation report: Orders failing at market open again

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** deadline · **Confidence:** 0.95 · **Written by:** reporting agent
> Honesty check: reported conclusive although the run stopped (deadline) without critic acceptance; the report gives a justification

## Summary
At market open on 2026-09-28 at 09:15 IST (03:45 UTC), stock order placements experienced high latency and failures with HTTP 503 errors. While initially suspected to be external broker API rate limiting or degradation similar to past incidents, investigation revealed that order-service exhausted its internal HTTP client connection pool to broker-connector (all 20/20 connections busy), causing 423 order requests to time out waiting to acquire a connection. This pool constriction was caused by change CHG-48221 deployed after market close on Friday 2026-09-25, which reduced broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20.

**Root cause:** Configuration change CHG-48221 reduced order-service's HTTP client connection pool limit to broker-connector (broker_client.max_connections_per_host) tenfold from 200 to 20. During the Monday market open surge at 09:15 IST (03:45 UTC)—the first high-volume trading burst under this configuration—the 20 client connections were immediately saturated, causing incoming order requests to time out waiting for an available client pool connection.

## Hypotheses
1. **HTTP client connection pool starvation on order-service towards broker-connector due to premature reduction of max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20** — `order-service`, config_change, confidence 0.95, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_10, ev_11, ev_14, ev_17, ev_20] · Contradicting: none
   - Change CHG-48221 reduced max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20 on Friday evening. Market open on Monday morning generated a burst of traffic (broker-connector request rate surged to 317.3 req/s), immediately saturating all 20 connections and generating 423 logged HTTP 503 errors stating 'timed out waiting for a connection to broker-connector (client pool 20/20 busy)'.
2. **External broker API rate limiting or upstream degradation during market open auction** — `broker-api`, upstream_dependency_degradation, confidence 0.05, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_7] · Contradicting: [ev_19, ev_21, ev_22, ev_23, ev_24]
   - Though past incidents PIR-2006 and PIR-2018 exhibited similar symptoms due to broker API rate limits and 5xx errors, broker-connector metrics showed p95 orders latency of only 206.7 ms at 03:45 UTC, rate_limited_count of 0 at 03:45 UTC, normal error rates (~0.32%), and zero ERROR logs from broker-connector.
3. **Database connection pool exhaustion or database lock contention during opening order burst** — `database`, capacity_saturation, confidence 0.01, ruled_out
   - Supporting: none · Contradicting: [ev_1, ev_2, ev_3, ev_4, ev_5, ev_6, ev_12, ev_13]
   - The primary database showed steady active connections (175.5), negligible lock wait time (4.03 ms), normal CPU utilization (36.11%), flat query volume, and order-service's database connection pool wait time peaked at only 5.57 ms.

## Facts
- On Friday 2026-09-25T13:00:00.000Z (18:30 IST), change CHG-48221 reduced order-service config broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20 to align with service mesh defaults. [ev_10]
- Between 2026-09-28T03:45:02.512Z and 04:18:59.345Z, order-service emitted 423 ERROR logs with status 503 stating 'order <ref> failed: timed out waiting for a connection to broker-connector (client pool 20/20 busy)'. [ev_11, ev_14]
- All 423 ERROR logs recorded on order-service across the investigation window matched this single connection pool saturation error pattern. [ev_14]
- order-service connects synchronously to broker-connector with a 2000 ms timeout, 0 retries, and an HTTP client pool limit of max 20 connections per host. [ev_17]
- broker-connector upstream p95 latency for orders was 206.7 ms at 03:45 UTC, and its error rate remained low at 0.32% during market open. [ev_19, ev_21]
- broker-connector rate_limited_count on the orders endpoint was 0 count/min at 03:45 UTC, peaking at only 0.6 count/min at 04:10 UTC. [ev_22]
- Database active connections, lock wait time, CPU utilization, and slow queries remained flat and normal throughout the 03:45 UTC order surge. [ev_3, ev_4, ev_5, ev_6, ev_12]
- order-service database pool wait time peaked at 5.57 ms at 03:45 UTC with mean of 3.03 ms. [ev_2]

## Inferences
- Because CHG-48221 was applied on Friday evening after market close, Monday 2026-09-28 09:15 IST (03:45 UTC) was the first market open trading burst subjected to the reduced connection pool limit of 20. [ev_10]
- Order failures were not caused by downstream broker-connector or external broker-api degradation, as upstream latency remained around 200 ms and no rate limit spikes occurred. [ev_19, ev_21, ev_22, ev_23]
- A pool limit of 20 concurrent connections is insufficient to support market open request rates (which reached 317.3 req/s at broker-connector), causing order-service's internal connection pool wait queue to exceed its timeout threshold. [ev_11, ev_14, ev_17, ev_20]

## Assumptions
- Market open order volume on Monday morning is substantially higher than weekend or off-market hours trading activity.

## Timeline
- **2026-09-25T13:00:00.000Z (2026-09-25 18:30 IST)** Change CHG-48221 completed on order-service, reducing broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 200 to 20. [ev_10]
- **2026-09-28T03:45:00.000Z (2026-09-28 09:15 IST)** Indian stock markets open; order traffic surges, reaching 317.3 req/s at broker-connector. [ev_20]
- **2026-09-28T03:45:02.512Z (2026-09-28 09:15:02 IST)** First HTTP 503 error logged on order-service: timed out waiting for connection to broker-connector with client pool 20/20 busy. [ev_11, ev_14]
- **2026-09-28T03:45:00.000Z - 04:18:59.000Z (09:15 - 09:48 IST)** 423 stock order requests fail on order-service due to internal HTTP client pool saturation. [ev_14]
- **2026-09-28T04:18:59.345Z (2026-09-28 09:48:59 IST)** Last HTTP 503 client pool timeout error recorded on order-service as opening order volume subsides. [ev_14]

## Confidence
0.95: Direct and exact match between configuration change CHG-48221 (reducing broker client pool to 20), service dependency definition (max 20 connections per host), and order-service's explicit ERROR logs citing 'client pool 20/20 busy'. Downstream broker and database metrics firmly rule out external degradation.

## Gaps
- Round 0 specialist T4 call was aborted due to budget/deadline before completion. (impact: Minimal impact; subsequent tool queries in round 0 (ev_19 to ev_24) retrieved the necessary broker-connector metrics and logs to evaluate upstream latency, error rate, and rate limits.)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Revert CHG-48221 or increase order-service configuration broker_client.max_connections_per_host from 20 back to 200 (or appropriately scaled capacity based on peak open concurrency). [ev_10, ev_11, ev_14, ev_17, ev_20]
  - Why: 20 connections is severely inadequate for market open peak concurrency (~300+ req/s), as demonstrated by 100% pool saturation and 423 timed-out orders.
  - Verify: Deploy updated configuration, verify client pool in-use metrics do not reach 100% capacity during market open bursts, and confirm zero 503 pool wait timeout errors in order-service logs.
- **[next]** Establish load testing and capacity benchmarking requirements for connection pool setting changes prior to deploying to production tier-1 trading services. [ev_10, ev_17]
  - Why: Standardizing service mesh connection limits across services without validating peak market open throughput risks recurring burst capacity failures.
  - Verify: Review deployment checklist and CI/CD policy requiring performance testing against market-open burst profiles for dependency connection configurations.
- **[later]** Add specific alerting on order-service for HTTP client connection pool utilization exceeding 80% and connection pool acquire timeouts. [ev_11, ev_14]
  - Why: Currently, client pool exhaustion manifested only as downstream 503 errors and was initially misattributed to external broker downtime.
  - Verify: Trigger test alert in staging when client pool saturation exceeds threshold and ensure on-call receives accurate diagnostic alert.

## Justification
Although the investigation halted due to deadline without critic review, the evidence conclusive links the failure to change CHG-48221. order-service's error logs explicitly cite 'client pool 20/20 busy', exactly matching the 20-connection limit set in CHG-48221 and the dependency graph. Downstream broker-connector metrics simultaneously rule out broker degradation.
